subject: Criteria commitment, test sprint plan, and MAP for Summa evaluation
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Moran <alex.moran@summahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Criteria commitment, test sprint plan, and MAP for Summa evaluation

Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As discussed, attaching a concise mutual action plan (MAP) draft and the initial acceptance-test inventory so we can lock the close timeline. High level ask: can you confirm the acceptance owners on your side and whether the deployment will be in your AWS account or through Redwood-hosted Dedicated? That affects the infra prep sprint below.

Summary (proposed):
- Success criteria (minimum pass):
  - Functional: domain-specific accuracy / concordance on 5 canonical prompts >= 92% (see test vectors in eval-test-cases.md).
  - Safety/precision: hallucination rate < 2% on edge-case set; false-positive PHI leakage = 0 for sampled prompts.
  - Performance: 95th percentile latency < 350ms for single-turn inference at 512-token context under baseline load; sustain 40 qps with <10% tail amplification during throughput run.
  - Cost: estimated inference spend <= $0.25 per 1k tokens on average for evaluation traffic (billing window TBD).
- Exit gates (must be green to proceed to production proof):
  1) Evidence ledger populated with run artifacts for 3 smoke runs (owner: Summa QA).
  2) Security checklist (SOC2 evidence) accepted by your security reviewer.
  3) Rollback plan and fallback model variant validated in canary.
- Acceptance tests (owners & dates):
  - E2E smoke (owner: Summa QA) — run by 2026-06-28.
  - Throughput ramp (owner: Redwood infra) — 2026-07-02.
  - Edge-case hallucination sweep (joint) — 2026-07-05.
  - Data retention & audit log verification (Summa Sec Ops) — 2026-07-06.

Attachments: MAP_Summa_v1.xlsx (MAP with owners & tasks), eval-test-cases.md (test vectors), SOC2-summary.pdf (high-level evidence we can provide).

Proposed close timeline (conditional on approvals above):
- Week 1 (infra & access): 2026-06-22 — 2026-06-25 — cloud account connection, API keys, initial dataset handoff.
- Week 2 (smoke + tuning): 2026-06-26 — 2026-07-02 — run smoke tests, iterate prompts, logging enabled.
- Week 3 (throughput & security): 2026-07-03 — 2026-07-09 — ramp to target throughput, finalize SOC2/retention artifacts.
- Decision: Go/No-go review meeting on 2026-07-10.

Please confirm owners (especially for Evidence & Security) and any hard dates or procurement milestones on your side. If everything aligns, I’ll lock the MAP and schedule the 07/10 decision.

Cheers,

Rachel Kim
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0243
Redwood Inference

--

Attachment: eval-test-cases.md (stated)
Attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf (stated)

Date: 2026-06-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Criteria commitment, test sprint plan, and MAP for Summa evaluation

Rachel —

Appreciate the clear plan. Priya and I reviewed the criteria; overall 👍. A few quick clarifications from Summa:

1) Owners: Priya will own Evidence ledger signoff (Summa QA). Our security reviewer (Samir Gupta) needs the SOC2 summary and a short runbook for incident response — can Redwood provide a 1-page runbook?
2) Baseline traffic: we’ll start with a 20 qps baseline during smoke (not 40) and then ramp to 40 if the smoke is clean. Can Redwood run the throughput ramp on July 2 for 20→40 qps?
3) Data: we will supply a de-identified sample dataset (5k records) by EOD Monday (2026-06-22). Please confirm ingestion format (JSONL).

We’re good to target the 07/10 decision meeting — Priya, Samir and our procurement lead (Molly Chen) will try to attend. One ask: can Redwood include a simple pass/fail matrix in the MAP (green/amber/red for each gate)? That will help our execs.

Thanks — will confirm owners formally once Samir confirms availability.

Best,
Alex
VP Product, Summa Health
alex.moran@summahealth.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Criteria commitment, test sprint plan, and MAP for Summa evaluation

Ben / Karthik —

Quick internal: Alex confirmed most items. Action items from our side:
- Ben: prepare the 1-page incident runbook and SOC2 evidence pointer doc; attach to MAP by EOD 6/22.
- Karthik: plan throughput run with infra team to support 20→40 qps ramp on 7/02; validate that p95 target is achievable at 512 tokens.
- I'll update the MAP with a simple RAG pass/fail matrix (green/amber/red) for each gate and send to Summa for sign-off.

Considerations: if Summa prefers the workload run in their VPC, we need to allocate a Dedicated connector slot and update pricing estimates — flagging for sales motion. Also, procurement (Molly) might request a 60-day SLA review window; hold the standard terms for now and I’ll loop in legal if that goes live.

Short reply from you both confirming owners and I’ll lock the MAP.

Rachel
Director, Solutions
